Hi Lydia —

Quick note as we approach the contract renewal window (current term ends 2025-11-30). Atlas has been growing usage nicely and you mentioned exploring an on‑prem / VPC-isolated footprint for regulated workloads.

Attached is an initial SOW draft outlining two options:
- Option A: Add two dedicated on‑prem clusters behind a customer-managed VPC (recommended for strict isolation).
- Option B: Single dedicated on‑prem cluster + strict tenancy controls for a phased rollout.

Couple of ask items so we can firm pricing:
1) Confirm expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrency (tokens/sec or requests/min).
2) Preferred term: do you want to extend to 24 or 36 months for committed capacity pricing?
3) Any procurement contact or PO timeline we should work to?

I'll loop in Vivek and Marissa to propose an architecture and mutual action plan once you confirm the capacity targets.

Best,
Soojin

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the SOW draft. A few clarifying points from my side before we get into architecture:

- Regulated data must remain on Atlas-owned hardware in our primary DC (east-us-1). We need VPC peering and strict network separation between the hosted and on‑prem clusters.
- For sizing: target workload is ~1200 concurrent inference sessions at peak (predictive triage workflows). Average prompt length ~400 tokens.
- Procurement will need an updated quote and an explicit line item for data separation / attestations.
- Can you surface SOC 2 evidence and the data residency controls for the on‑prem option?

Looping procurement and Kevin (network ops) to coordinate their requirements. Please include estimated monthly GPU hours and a rough cost delta between Option A and B.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-15T14:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Renewal notice + proposal: on-prem expansion & isolation options

Thanks — technical reply with estimates below.

Summary recommendation (based on 1200 concurrent sessions, 400 token avg):
- Deploy two dedicated on‑prem clusters (primary + warm standby) to cover failover and maintenance windows. Each cluster: 8x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent), load balanced by local LB.
- KV/prefix cache placed in‑cluster (on‑prem) to meet latency SLOs and prevent cross‑tenant cache exposure.
- VPC peering + strict routed subnets, firewall rules to restrict control-plane egress to Redwood-owned service IPs over mTLS.

Estimated monthly GPU hours (steady-state): ~9,600 GPU-hours across both clusters.
Cost delta (ballpark): Option A (two clusters): +$92k/month vs current hosted spend. Option B (single cluster phased): +$48k/month initially, with a migration uplift later.

Risks / mitigations:
- Networking complexity: validate port whitelists and peering routes with Kevin.
- Upgrade paths: recommend embedded maintenance windows and canary rollouts (Redwood supports canary deploys to avoid region-wide regressions).

I’m happy to run a quick 30-min call with Atlas network ops to walk the diagram and confirm port requirements.

Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
